item.text: {"question_id":"3B.4","answer":"In 2023, the government had formal justice, complaint, monitoring, and victim-reparation mechanisms, but their independence, implementation, and corrective effectiveness were limited. Positive evidence includes legislation establishing a victim-support commission and fund with access-to-justice, compensation, legal-assistance, and mediation functions; recruitment and training of magistrates; mobile-court judgments; police investigative-capacity work; and a National Commission on Human Rights that issued reports, visited detention centers, trained magistrates, and followed up on civilian complaints (BATCH-0029-E001; BATCH-0009-E004; BATCH-0011-E014). The government also permitted some domestic and international monitoring, and the state prosecuted some security personnel, including convictions arising from the Goma killings (BATCH-0011-E008; BATCH-0011-E014; BATCH-0011-E021). However, judicial independence was weakened by political and military interference, corruption, resource shortfalls, and presidential appointment, removal, retirement, and reassignment of judges and prosecutors whose effects on independence are unestablished (BATCH-0028-E017; BATCH-0015-E006). Authorities denied UN access to some military and intelligence detention sites, and the National Commission and Human Rights Ministry lacked full provincial representation and struggled with effectiveness (BATCH-0011-E014). The Goma case shows serious limits in investigation and remedy: no adequate scene evidence, ballistic investigation, or autopsies; incomplete victim identification; missing persons; restricted witnesses and appeal access; flawed civilian prosecutions; and a reparations order whose payment is not established (BATCH-0011-E020; BATCH-0011-E021). The legal reparations framework therefore demonstrates formal design, not funded or delivered remedy. The ICC cooperation agreement and stated rule-of-law commitment are external accountability cooperation and political commitments, not evidence of effective independent domestic oversight; no implementation outcome is supplied (BATCH-0019-E001; BATCH-0019-E002).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0029-E001","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0011-E014","BATCH-0011-E021"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E008","BATCH-0011-E020","BATCH-0028-E017","BATCH-0015-E006","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0019-E002"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not establish nationwide independence or effectiveness of courts and complaint systems.","The victim-reparation law does not establish 2023 disbursement, staffing, or geographic reach; the Goma reparations order does not establish payment.","Many accountability measures are attributed to government institutions rather than personally to Tshisekedi.","The Goma death toll and some investigative conclusions remain disputed, and appeals were pending.","The evidence does not establish that judicial appointments or reshuffles produced either independence or interference in specific cases."],"corrections_made":["Removed the ICC agreement and investigation request as positive evidence of domestic courts, complaint systems, or remedy; retained them only as external-cooperation and commitment evidence with explicit limits.","Separated formal legal design and institutional outputs from demonstrated independence, compliance, effective investigation, and delivered victim remedy.","Preserved both accountability actions and contrary evidence of judicial interference, restricted access, flawed investigations, collective or individualized-evidence concerns, and incomplete remedy."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
